Usage and limitations: Define agents, tools, data and transitions in a versionable file. A deterministic graph does not make LLM responses identical.
Canvas, node library, inspector, live validation, undo and redo.
Starter templates, mission form, parameters and a first run; equivalent creation through the CLI.
Deterministic ZIP archive containing the workflow, prompts, skills, attachments and manifest; supports declaring a minimum engine version.
Parameterize a method at launch and distribute specializations without copying the entire workflow.
Create, duplicate and edit bundle files in cloud Studio, with conflict checks on save.
Static converter from Claude JavaScript files to a .bot draft, with a report of unsupported elements. Does not import n8n workflows.

Validate references, properties and graph/data-flow constraints before execution. General node-output schema validation is an engine option, not enabled by product entry points in this build; compute outputs are checked separately.
Generate a compact, detailed or full workflow diagram for documentation and review.
Separate production from evaluation in the graph; a judge is a configurable LLM evaluation, not proof of correctness.
Command nodes or JavaScript, Python and shell/Bash scripts, with stdout capture and error handling.

Feature: Computation without a model or shell
Usage and limitations: The compute node provides bounded expressions, transformations, map/filter/reduce and typed outputs.
Select a branch using rules, a model decision or a declared rotation.
fan_out_all, fan_out_each, with wait_all or best_effort collection; concurrent workspace writes are restricted.

Feature: Bounded, data-driven loops and ordered iteration
Usage and limitations: Fixed or data-resolved bounds, foreach, and explicit unbounded loops governed by fuel and a stagnation monitor. Empty foreach input requires a guard if its body must never run.
Declare a subgraph and instantiate it with distinct parameters and prefixes.
Call another bot, retrieve its output and isolate its work; budgets, memory and supervisors have parent/child limitations.
Declare resources and reserve a slot with needs, for example to limit simultaneous worktrees.

Feature: Emitting and waiting for internal events
Usage and limitations: In-run emit/wait, retained events for late waiters and mandatory timeouts. Durable parking on external events is deferred.
claw, claude_code, pi, codex, kimi, grok, with different capabilities and support levels.

Feature: Model and backend selection per node
Usage and limitations: Mix executors in one workflow, select the model independently of the backend and apply launch overrides.
Configurable fallback chains when the initial access is unsuitable; changes should remain observable.
Declare a fallback executor or a workflow-defined skip route; prerequisites are validated. Codex is excluded from the first cross-backend fallback version.
Choose conversational continuity between steps; session resume and fork are not wired for Kimi/Grok.
session: persist reuses a node's conversation in a loop; supported on Claude Code, pi and Codex along the main workflow path.
artifacts_only passes the useful result without carrying the previous step's conversation history.
Configurable threshold and retention of recent exchanges; depends on the executor and can support error recovery.
Qualitative or numeric prompt settings for depth, caution, style and more. They guide the model without enforcing permissions or guaranteeing quality.
Choose reasoning_effort per node or through input data; levels adapt to model and backend support, independently of behavior dials.

Feature: Sub-agents and workflows created within a node
Usage and limitations: ultracode enables dynamic orchestration on claw and Claude Code depending on model, harness and tools; separate from declared fan-out and sub-bots. Pi does not provide this capability.
human nodes support text, choices, booleans, numbers and lists; review context is separate from expected answers.
ask_user with answers through Studio, CLI or API; support depends on backend and transport.
ask_user_async lets the agent continue before receiving answers; asynchronous interaction runs on the main path, outside fan-out branches.
await_answers synchronizes pending questions; the node requires a timeout, and the run remains active while waiting.
llm and llm_or_human modes follow workflow policy; an automated answer is not human approval.

Feature: Guidance added to an active run
Usage and limitations: Inbox and steering redirect work at backend-defined intake points; they do not instantly cancel an ongoing action.

Feature: Files and images at launch or in an answer
Usage and limitations: Persisted attachments with MIME type, size and hash; vision depends on the model. Review gates do not accept the same uploads as ordinary human nodes.
Review companion, correction requests and an optional review environment; explicitly choose human_required or an agent verdict.
Request a pause at the next safe boundary, then resume; local in-process path only, with remote cloud pause unimplemented.
Observe an agent/judge node and inject guidance during execution; supervisors declared inside sub-bots are not currently wired.
React to events, errors or cost signals with a cooldown and evaluation limit; account for supervision costs.

Feature: Attaching a supervisor to a session
Usage and limitations: Attach through the CLI to a local run, or to a Claude Code session with prepared transcript and hooks; remote cloud attachment is deferred.

Feature: Changing budgets and iterations during a run
Usage and limitations: Raise limits or grant extra iterations with acknowledgment and a recorded event; changes apply at safe boundaries.
Retain knowledge as Markdown documents beyond a single run's artifacts.
Private run, bot, project, multiple projects, user, organization and global catalog; storage and context determine access. Global scope is read-only for organizations.

Feature: Agent memory read, write and list tools
Usage and limitations: memory_read, memory_write, memory_list, with configurable permissions; check the adapter and backend in use.
Inject an index, preload selected documents and reinject memory before compaction according to configuration.
auto_memory maintains a MEMORY.md per bot and repository; opt-in on claw/Claude Code/pi, with restrictions for cloud sandboxes without read-back.
Aggregate, space and document quotas; structured secret detection does not cover all confidential data.
tar.gz archives through CLI/API, with skip, overwrite or rename strategies to retain or transfer knowledge.
Global, project or bundled skills; management CLI and local editor, with selected skills transported to cloud runners.

Feature: Skills selected per workflow or node
Usage and limitations: Name and description enter the context; content loads on demand. A missing skill produces a warning.
MCP, skills, output rewriting, commands, agents, hooks and lifecycle features; backend support varies by contribution.
Resolve private and public sources, then transport them for local or cloud runs.
RTK plugin and compress modes reduce text sent to the model; plugin availability and activation depend on the interface in use.
Declare MCP servers, inherit them or disable them per node; transports and support depend on the backend.
iterion mcp exposes launch, monitoring, human answers and board operations, locally or against a configured remote instance.
Native tools or configured providers/MCP, including DuckDuckGo, Brave, SearXNG and Firecrawl; coverage varies by backend.

Feature: Deterministic connector actions and package generation
Usage and limitations: Local in-process action: nodes use typed parameters, bound connections and structured results with pagination/completion indicators. Generate packages from OpenAPI/Swagger with an authored overlay. Project catalogs require opt-in; cloud transport and the catalog MCP facade are outside this delivered scope.
Resume eligible states with outputs, counters and position; interrupted steps may execute again.
Reattach the parent to its recorded child run instead of always launching a new child, when the state is recoverable.
rewind invalidates dependent outputs; --auto locates a changed node. Branch and starting-state restrictions apply.
Filesystem tracker wired to local CLI/Studio, with deduplicated states at execution boundaries; cloud runners do not wire this tracker. Separate from pushed Git workspace checkpoints.
Restore run-produced files from available local snapshots while protecting operator changes; ignored or oversized paths are excluded.
Check a condition before and after a command, skip an already-satisfied action and select required/recover/best_effort policy.
Propose a corrected command, then optionally delegate recovery to an agent; opt-in, bounded attempts, with success determined by the postcondition.
Error classification, backoff, compaction or human pause; optional CLI auto-resume excludes terminal errors.
Expose the last successfully pushed workspace checkpoint and a recovery command; this does not automatically restore files or validate a deliverable.

Feature: Forking a run from an earlier exchange
Usage and limitations: Create a resumable run with modified inputs and restore the code snapshot when available; conversational precision depends on the backend.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Isolate a run's Git changes; behavior depends on mode and repository, particularly for empty repositories.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Retain or integrate the result according to the selected policy; finalization authority must be granted.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Review, corrections and merge/squash decision within the supported flow; configure acceptance criteria and the target branch.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Inspect modified files, diffs and commits from a run; metadata is persisted for documented cloud paths.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Bounded collection of eligible old worktrees preserves dirty, active or recoverable work; it is not a strict disk cap.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Prepare tooling declared by the bot and repository; requires a compatible installation and execution environment.

Category: 🌿 Working and delivering in a repository
Usage and limitations: Guided forge connection, target selection and authorized creation in cloud Studio. Manifests also support optional or no repository requirements; creation needs forge permissions.
Declare forge, command, schedule, board and keepalive inputs, with direct launch or card creation.
GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea or generic payloads; configurable event/project/author filters and authentication.
Slash commands and bot replies in authorized GitHub/GitLab threads; replies still rely on a skill, while native forge.reply is deferred.
Cron, guards and overlap policy; runs through host cron locally or the platform scheduler.
Relaunch recurring missions using guards and availability windows; configure behavior per bot and backend.

Feature: Triggers on events and run outcomes
Usage and limitations: Subscribe to board events, explicit events or run completion to chain missions.

Feature: Durable outbox for cloud board effects
Usage and limitations: Materialization, claim, retry and permanent failure for trigger effects; at-least-once execution with documented residual failure windows.
Policy frozen at launch for merge, relaunch or escalation; server option and decision log.
HMAC-signed completion callbacks, operator alerts and Web Push require configuration; native desktop notifications are deferred.

Feature: Native kanban independent of a forge
Usage and limitations: Cards, columns, labels, priorities, assignments and comments through Studio or CLI.
Validated card schema, hard blockers and waiting_deps state prevent premature launches.
Selection, claim, launch, retries, stall detection and concurrency limits; native tracker and configurable adapters.
View planned tasks and active runs, launch by priority and limit concurrent pipelines.
Bidirectional statuses; issue fields synchronize according to a specific mapping, not arbitrary field replication.

Feature: Links between cards, runs and results
Usage and limitations: Latest run, worktree, wait states and event history establish work provenance.
Share revocable access to selected repository file fields; forge commits, conflict checks and audit, without operator Studio access.
Ask/deny gates on agent calls: claw, Claude Code and pi RPC; Kimi/Grok deny only, Codex without this gate. permission: does not apply to shell tool nodes.
Configurable isolation by backend, driver and deployment; auto can degrade, while Codex uses its own sandbox.
Bindings limit supplied secrets; allowed_hosts covers supported egress paths. This guarantee does not extend to every shell call.
AES-256-GCM with record binding; authorized cloud components share the key. Automatic master-key rotation is not currently available.
Materialize a secret with as: file, with in-run refresh on supported paths.
Go-based privacy_filter covers accounts, emails, phone numbers, URLs and secrets. Person names, postal addresses and dates are excluded.

privacy_unfilter restores original values if the vault file is retained; the vault is not replicated to Mongo/S3. Trace masking targets privacy_filter inputs and privacy_unfilter outputs, not data flowing elsewhere.
MIME, size, path and SSRF controls on covered routes; active content is restricted, without a general guarantee that files are harmless.
macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service integration requires the system service. Separate from cloud secret sealing.
Separate platform resources by tenant and assign operator/administrator permissions and editing capabilities.
Generic OIDC and dedicated connectors, with organization-specific configuration and access policies.
BYOK, defaults and launch/integration overrides follow the resolution chain; providers bill separately.
Reuse authentication supported by CLI backends within the limits of those accounts and their providers.
Credential lending with audience, availability, limits and per-run leases; does not increase provider quotas.

Feature: Run budgets: cost, tokens, duration and iterations
Usage and limitations: Configurable limits, backend-dependent estimates, finalization headroom and separate sub-bot budgets; not a universal billing cap.
Concurrency, rate, monthly and cost quotas; quota reads can allow a launch through on storage errors.
Adjustable soft/hard thresholds and policies; measurement is currently specific to Claude Code and separate from monetary budgets.
Attributed API access and administrative actions; change history covers supported operations.
Launch displays backend, permission, compression and auto-memory values and provenance, plus nodes with their own settings.
Graph, events, logs and counters for monitoring execution in Studio.
Versioned outputs and persisted events for inspecting completed runs.
Breakdown by model/provider, run counts, failures and P50/P95 durations; precision depends on available accounting.
Deterministic TodoWrite/todo_write history reconstructed from events; currently populated by Claude Code and claw.
Notes, metrics, checklists, progress and charts; local opt-in with an evaluation budget, not currently wired to cloud.
Result URLs, run-linked captures and live browser through manual local attachment; cloud live browsing and Playwright auto-attach are deferred.
A tool can publish a generated file as a run attachment using a stdout directive; publication failures are reported without failing the tool.
Inspect an idle run in its retained environment; local Unix only, without a cloud host terminal.
Process JSON, alerts and Sentry/GlitchTip integration; a DSN is required and tracing is enabled separately.
Metrics endpoint and supplied observability stack; costs, tokens, retries and durations depend on data exposed by each backend.
Edit a text file in a retained local worktree; 4 MiB limit, without Git staging, locking or concurrent conflict checks. Separate from the bot editor.

Feature: CLI, Studio, desktop app and self-hosted cloud
Usage and limitations: Multiple interfaces around the same engine; feature parity is incomplete.
NATS queue, runners, MongoDB and S3 storage; Kubernetes architecture and scaling require operation.

Feature: Bot sources frozen at cloud launch
Usage and limitations: Hashed snapshot of parent, sub-bots and resources; runners do not silently substitute their own catalog version.
Control runs, resume and consume events; documented SDK support for Node, Deno and Bun.
Combine workflow, parameters, prompts, budgets and evaluation policy into benchmark campaigns.
bench asymptote aggregates verdicts by iteration without replaying LLMs; it neither guarantees convergence nor constitutes a completed competitive benchmark.
Modifiable, self-hostable engine; third-party components and services retain their own terms.
Select and return to multiple projects in the native app; onboarding prepares a first project.
Verify the manifest and artifact using Ed25519, then offer installation according to package and platform. This does not imply macOS notarization or Windows signing.
app-dev, feature-dev, feature-gap-fill, bmady bundles; workflows adaptable to the repository and acceptance criteria.
review-pr, revi-converse and review helpers; verify forge coverage and permissions.
whole-improve-loop, branch-improve-loop, modernize, evolve; each bot defines its checks and approval steps.
test-coverage, e2e-coverage, golden-master, instrument build or inspect evidence suited to the project.
sec-audit-source, sec-audit-deps, dep-update-guard, secured-renovacy, supply-shield and variants; an automated audit cannot certify the absence of vulnerabilities.
vuln-watch detects issues and routes remediation according to configuration.
rgaa-audit, ultra11y; assess audits and fixes against the tested scope, without assuming automatic compliance.
docs-refresh, product-docs, wiki-gen, adr-cartograph, adr-rechallenge produce and update documents for review.
feed-watch, issue-triage, whats-next, campaign; collection, synthesis and coordination using the supplied workflows.
